thread:
Mira Patel: Starting a quiet-window publish for py/ts SDKs. Plan: canary -> staged dist-tag -> GA. Canary will be 20% for 2h, smoke, then 80% staged for 4h if green. No automatic promotions without explicit +1.
Aj Chen: Ack. I'll watch signing & npm publish.
deploy-bot: [Automated] queued: build and publish pipeline for packages: @redwood/sdk-py 0.5.3-canary, @redwood/sdk-ts 0.5.3-canary. CI run #4578 started.
Santiago Rivera: seeing a failing integration in the TS client smoke: `fetch-concurrency` test flakes on node 18 only. Not sure it's release-blocking but worth noting.
Kate Liu: heads-up: signing service returned a checksum mismatch earlier when uploading wheels to staging. Holding promotion.
Aj Chen: I can confirm the wheel checksum mismatch for 0.5.3-canary on staging. Hold promotion until we validate signer.
Mira Patel: Hold. Do not promote any dist-tags ('canary' -> 'next' -> 'latest') yet. Share reproducer/logs pls.
Santiago Rivera: log snippet:
``` 
error: signature verification failed: signer_id mismatch (expected: rsa-2023-01, got: rsa-2024-03)
artifact: sdk_py-0.5.3-cp39-cp39-manylinux2014.whl
```
Kate Liu: that's the signing key rotation we planned but the CI didn't pick the new key. Re-running signing job after rotation. ETA ~30m.
deploy-bot: [Automated] action: promotion to 'next' for @redwood/sdk-ts canceled due to validation failure.
Aj Chen: proposal: increment patch to 0.5.4-canary, rotate signing keys properly in CI, republish both wheels and npm tarball to a new canary tag `canary-042`, pin internal cohort 'canary-internal' to test.
Mira Patel: +1 to republish flow but we do not GA until the TS flaky test is addressed. Also update the release notes draft and mark the legacy sync client deprecation note so docs team can prep.
Kate Liu: signing rotated and new artifacts uploaded: py 0.5.4-canary, ts 0.5.4-canary. Checksums uploaded to staging.
deploy-bot: [Automated] publish started for artifacts: 0.5.4-canary (job #4590).
Aj Chen: I'll shepherd the npm publish and pin the npm `canary-042` dist-tag to cohort. Ping me if npm publish fails.
Santiago Rivera: rerunning extended smoke tests against the canary cohort now. Running the flaky test in a loop to verify fix PR.
Mira Patel: Rollback criteria for this rollout: - >1% error rate on 50+ requests in 10m window OR - any sustained 5xx spike (>5 in 10m). If triggered, yank canary, revert dist-tags, and cut hotfix if needed.
Aj Chen: timeline: republish done, smoke 2h. If green -> staged 80% for 4h, then GA next change window.
deploy-bot: [Automated] hold placed by Mira Patel. Notification sent to #incidents for visibility.
Kate Liu: done: publishing succeeded for 0.5.4-canary, checksums match, dist-tags still blocked for promote.
Santiago Rivera: smoke tests running. Initial 10m looks ok, flaky test passed 50/50 earlier; will keep monitoring.
Mira Patel: Thanks. I'll update the release-notes draft and add the deprecation blurb for the legacy sync client (next major). I'll also add the rollback criteria to the release playbook.
Aj Chen: once we hit staged and are stable, plan a short canary->ga sync to confirm rollout window and docs release.
Kate Liu: FYI to support: pause automated reminder emails for users who opted into canary telemetry until after staged.
Mira Patel: Nice. If anything spikes, call the rollback and ping the oncall.
Aj Chen: Roger. I'll stay online for the next 4 hours.
Mira Patel: Sweet. Team, please post any weird client-side errors here so we can decide quickly. :thumbsup:
